title: Vasaloppet Base Endurance - Steady State Cardio

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly and deliberately, syncing movement with breath. Focus on spinal mobility and core activation.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Control the movement, keeping hips level. This opens hip flexors and external rotators crucial for endurance athletes.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Hold each side for 30 seconds minimum. Keep heel planted and lean forward to feel the stretch in the calf.

items.name: Agility Ladder Run
items.cues: Light, controlled footwork through ladder drills. Focus on quick cadence and foot placement. Build heart rate gradually.

items.name: Air Bike - Steady State Endurance
items.cues: Maintain RPE 5-6 (conversational pace). You should be able to speak in sentences but not sing. Steady, rhythmic breathing. Aim for consistent cadence around 80-100 RPM. This builds aerobic base essential for 90km race.

items.name: Air Bike - Easy Recovery Spin
items.cues: Very light resistance, RPE 2-3. Allow heart rate to gradually decrease. This active recovery helps with blood lactate clearance.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Hold 30 seconds per side. Gently rotate torso away to deepen stretch in shoulders and chest.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Move slowly and controlled. Focus on core stability and breath. Alternate sides smoothly.

rationale: Returning from extended rest (999 days) after no recent training requires a conservative restart at RPE 5-6, allowing aerobic base development without excessive fatigue or injury risk.
Vasaloppet 90km is a long-distance endurance event requiring sustained aerobic capacity. This 45-minute steady-state session builds the critical base fitness needed with 53 days until race.
Gym-based Air Bike provides controlled, repeatable endurance training that minimizes injury risk while delivering the cardiovascular stimulus needed for cross-country ski performance.
